To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure and dynamics play a critical role in determining the binding affinity of the MBPs for their respective ligands.
the three isoforms of the MBP from T. maritima (tmMBP) are high-affinity binding proteins for di-, tri- and tetrasaccha-rides.

tmMBPs are able to differentiate between a variety of substrates, which is enabled by differences in the size of the binding pocket as well as the magnitude of the hinge-bending motions that they undergo upon substrate binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of substrate recognition by maltose binding protein isoforms.
how the structure and dynamical properties influence substrate recognition in the MBP family of proteins.
understanding how proteins can differentiate between similar substrates and how this can be related to their structure and dynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tmMBP1/2 have larger substrate binding pockets and undergo larger substrate-induced conformational changes, which enables them to bind a wider range of substrates than tmMBP3.
the binding site size and the ability of the protein to undergo substrate-induced conformational changes are key factors in substrate recognition.

the binding pockets of the three tmMBP isoforms differ in size, and that the hinge bending motions are different in magnitude, and that these two properties enable the three isoforms to differentiate between a variety of chemical entities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the substrate binding pockets and hinge bending motions of the MBP isoforms are the primary determinants of substrate selectivity and affinity.
tmMBP1 is more promiscuous than tmMBP2 or tmMBP3.
the thermophilic tmMBPs are highly selective for their substrates, while the mesophilic ecMBP is less selective and can bind to a wider variety of substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
substrate binding and dynamics are important factors in the evolution of protein specificity.
substrate recognition is influenced by the structural properties of binding pockets, which in turn is influenced by the dynamics of the proteins.
the substrate binding pocket of MBP is not the only factor that determines substrate specificity.
